Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the signature this morning. Per our call, attached is the first draft of the mutual action plan (MAP) with the implementation playlist embedded: rollout milestones, canary cadence, migration windows, and training scope. I pushed a copy to the shared Drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdPolarisMAP (sheet is "PolarisPay_MAP_v0.9.xlsx").

Top-level proposal (high level):
- Provisioning: week of 11/20 — dedicated tenant and SSO config
- Canary: 2-week canary starting 11/27 (25% traffic, runbook + rollback criteria)
- Migration: progressive routing 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks after canary
- Training & enablement: train-the-trainer + internal shadow sessions during canary window

Evaluation plan (embedded in the MAP):
- Tech checks: 99th P90 latency target < 200ms (in-region), error rate < 0.5%
- Quality checks: closed-set evaluation (50 canonical prompts) with automated scoring + manual spot-checks; target 92% pass rate on acceptance suite
- Ops checks: roll-forward metrics, cache hit rate, and budget burn estimates

Action items for PolarisPay: please confirm the procurement sign-off target date and the primary point-of-contact for training. I attached the draft MAP and an implementation checklist.

Attachments: PolarisPay_MAP_v0.9.xlsx, implementation-checklist.pdf

Thanks — available for a quick 30-min sync if you want to walk the sheet.

—

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: internal: PolarisPay MAP — timeline options and canary runbook

Team — following Alyssa's note, I've sketched an adjusted cadence that accommodates a later procurement sign-off and keeps our risk controls tight. Key points below; I'm attaching a concise runbook excerpt to the thread (implementation-checklist.pdf).

Proposed adjusted timeline (option A, aligned with PolarisPay ask):
- 11/20: Redwood completes tenant provisioning (holds) and pushes SSO metadata to PolarisPay
- 11/27-12/03: dry run & test harness (no traffic) — connectivity, load tests, KV cache warm-up
- 12/04-12/17: canary window (14 days) at 25% traffic; daily smoke checks and 3-day manual quality spot-checks
- 12/18-12/31: progressive migration (50% -> 100%) with monitored ramp and rollback gates

Acceptance & rollback criteria (short):
- Performance: 95th latency < 150ms average; if 95th exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive measurement windows (1 hour each) we pause ramp
- Errors: sustained error rate > 0.5% for >30 minutes -> instant rollback to previous routing
- Quality: automated eval drop > 4 points vs baseline or > 6% of spot-checks failing -> pause and manual triage

Evaluation plan specifics (what we'll deliver):
- Hosted evaluation harness that injects canonical test prompts and mirrors a subset of production traffic (sanitized)
- Daily scorecard (latency, errors, pass rate, cost burn) published to the MAP sheet
- Training plan: two 90-min instructor-led sessions during week 1 of canary + shadowing schedule for 3 ops users

Owners:
- Runbook & canary orchestration: Jonas Weber
- Quality/eval harness: Marcus Lin
- Security evidence & retention config: Neha Kapoor (SOC2 artifacts)
- Primary CS lead & customer communication: Maya Srinivasan

If procurement pushes hard to 11/20 sign-off, we can accelerate provisioning but must keep the dry-run week to avoid surprises. Thoughts?

— Jonas
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
